transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-22 10:00 PDT | Duration: 45min | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Aisha Patel (BlueWave ML Eng), Tom Reynolds (BlueWave Infra), Sofia Gomez (BlueWave Product)

Summary: quick recap of numbers from last week, Diego ran a small internal test and increased KV cache size + adjusted prefix hashing. Main ask today: validate hit-rate gains on customer workload and finalize bench plan.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have about 45 minutes. quick agenda: diego will walk through the tuned config and the hit rates, then we discuss prompt reuse strategy and next steps.
[00:25] Aisha Patel: sounds good, i just wanna say we had a couple of high-latency tails in the last run, so if we can keep an eye on 95th that'd be great.
[00:34] Diego Ramos: yep, noted. quick note though - numbers i'm about to share are from a 100k token sim on our side with the sample traces you gave, it's not full 24h but should be indicative.
[00:50] Diego Ramos: ok so baseline before tuning was prefix hit-rate about 12% overall, KV cache hit-rate around 22% and p95 latency ~420ms on our hosted cluster. after the X-LRU tweaks and increasing KV cache from 8GB to 16GB we saw prefix hit-rate up to ~28% and KV up to 46%, p95 dropped to ~320ms.
[01:18] Tom Reynolds: those numbers look promising. question - what's the memory footprint change? doubling KV cache sounds heavy for our tight host budget.
[01:26] Diego Ramos: rough calc - for your model mix it increased effective memory by ~9GB per node; there's also a CPU overhead for the new hashing buckets but small. we can tradeoff by shrinking TTLs or adding an adaptive eviction for cold prefixes.
[01:45] Sofia Gomez: can you explain the prefix buckets again, i think we missed some of the detail last time.
[01:52] Diego Ramos: sure, so we bucket prefixes by normalized prompt fingerprint - basically we hash the normalized prompt up to the first 128 tokens, that way paraphrases map to the same bucket if normalization matches. each bucket keeps a small LRU of KV entries and a compact sketch for popularity. the X-LRU means we keep two tiers: sticky hot prefixes and transient prefixes.
[02:18] Aisha Patel: normalization - are you doing aggressive canonicalization? we have a lot of templated prompts with variables so we want reuse across different user ids.
[02:27] Diego Ramos: yes we strip IDs, timestamps, non-semantic tokens; we also support rules you can add (we can take your prompt templates and generate rules). caveat: aggressive normalization risks collision where semantically distinct prompts get merged, so we recommend test set validation.
[02:46] Maya Chen: okay and what's the false-hit rate tradeoff? are we seeing any incorrect reuse where content is reused but should not be?
[02:54] Diego Ramos: on the sim it's low, maybe <1.5% of retrieved KV entries were semantically off for the eval prompts. again real world might differ. we can add a similarity threshold check before reusing cached KVs - that slows things a bit but keeps quality.
[03:10] Tom Reynolds: is that the similarity check that runs on the vector embeddings? how expensive is that?
[03:18] Diego Ramos: it's a cheap dot-prod on small vectors, maybe adds ~8-12ms on average per decision; you can do it asynchronously for best-effort reuse too.
[03:28] Aisha Patel: what about TTLs? we saw early evictions caused low reuse during bursts.
[03:34] Diego Ramos: we changed TTL strategies: for very high-frequency prefixes we set longer TTL (up to 1h), for mid-frequency 10-15m, for low-frequency 30s. TTLs were auto-bucketed by observed qps. that improved hit-rate a lot in the sim.
[03:57] Sofia Gomez: does that mean we need to pre-warm caches if we have known campaigns or new prompts?
[04:03] Diego Ramos: pre-warming helps; we also do lazy warming on first use and background fill when you see a pattern. for launches we recommend a short warm-up window with synthetic traffic.
[04:15] Aisha Patel: can we control these settings from Console? our infra team wants a single toggle.
[04:21] Maya Chen: yes Diego - are those exposed?
[04:24] Diego Ramos: currently via config file and API, dashboard toggle is in roadmap but not GA. we can share the config snippet and a one-line curl to apply.
[04:33] Tom Reynolds: next on perf: tail latencies - did the p99 change?
[04:37] Diego Ramos: p99 improved modestly from ~520ms to ~470ms in sim; the biggest wins were p75-p95. p99 needs more aggressive overprovisioning or dedicated nodes to avoid cold-starts.
[04:52] Aisha Patel: that matches what we saw, our p99 spikes during rare flows. might be okay for now.
[04:58] Sofia Gomez: prompt reuse strategy - we have templates where variable slots are replaced. what's the recommended approach for BlueWave product prompts?
[05:05] Diego Ramos: recommended: canonicalize templates into stable keys, enforce a small set of variable types (IDs, dates) and register them, then use prefix hashing on the canonical key plus the bucketed suffix. for slot-heavy templates, reuse tends to be lower so consider more aggressive normalization.
[05:23] Maya Chen: Aisha - would you be able to share a sanitized sample of your production prompt set and a 24h traffic sample so we can run the full bench?
[05:30] Aisha Patel: yes we can strip PII and upload. we'll aim for end of week.
[05:34] Maya Chen: great. Diego, what's the bench plan and timeline?
[05:37] Diego Ramos: plan: run an end-to-end 1M-token run with the new X-LRU + similarity filter off, then repeat with similarity filter on, capture token cost, hit rates by prefix classes, p50/p95/p99. target to finish by 9/29 and share raw logs and dashboard link.
[05:56] Tom Reynolds: can you also provide the config snippet and expected memory overhead per node? we need to validate with our infra team.
[06:02] Diego Ramos: yes will include per-node mem delta and a recommended memory limit.
[06:08] Maya Chen: pricing - i'll send an updated pilot pricing note factoring in expected cache savings, should help the procurement conversation.
[06:13] Sofia Gomez: curious if we should consider dedicated for this pilot to avoid noisy neighbors if hit-rates look good.
[06:19] Diego Ramos: dedicated helps tail and predictable throughput; if your p99 requirements tighten then dedicated or reserved capacity is the hop. we can model costs both hosted+cache and dedicated.
[06:30] Aisha Patel: any security implications with KV caching? data residency?
[06:34] Diego Ramos: we keep KV in-memory on serving nodes, can encrypt at rest for optional swap, audit logs for cache ops available, and private deployment/VPC option also supports KMS. we'll include the security note in the doc pack.
[06:50] Maya Chen: alright let's recap quick.
[06:53] Maya Chen: next steps: Diego runs 1M token bench (due 9/29), Diego shares config snippet and mem numbers (due 9/24), Maya sends updated pricing (due 9/24), BlueWave uploads sanitized prompts + 24h traffic (due 9/25).
[07:10] Aisha Patel: sounds good, and we'll review results and decide on whether to expand cache sizes or move to dedicated.
[07:17] Tom Reynolds: one more ask - can the bench include a run that simulates a launch (burst) to see cache warm behavior?
[07:22] Diego Ramos: yes, i'll add a synthetic burst scenario as a second run.
[07:26] Maya Chen: perfect. anyone else?
[07:28] Sofia Gomez: no, thanks.
[07:29] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, will follow up with notes and the pricing doc. bye.

Notes on transcript quality: some names and technical terms may be slightly off (e.g., X-LRU vs XLru in auto-transcript), timestamps approximate.
